newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-LATE GOAL GIVES CZECHS BRONZE CONSOLATION.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-LATE GOAL GIVES CZECHS BRONZE CONSOLATION.

text.p: Jiri Dopita hit a powerplay goal with less than two minutes left to earn the Czech Republic a 4-3 win over Russia and the world ice hockey championship bronze medal on Saturday.
The bronze will be a consolation prize for the Czechs, who failed to defend successfully the title they won last year in Vienna.
Canada will take on Sweden in the best-of-three final beginning Sunday.
It was a disappointing end to the championship for the Russians, who came within a goal of a place in the final, losing 2-1 to Canada on Friday.
The loss also marked the fourth consecutive year the once feared Russians, who as the Soviet Union dominated the championship by winning 20 titles, returned home without a medal.

Dopita, unmarked just off the Russian goalcrease, scooped up the rebound off Robert Reichel's slapshot and hammered it past a helpless Mixim Mikhailovski to give the Czechs their fourth bronze medal in the last eight championships.
The goal checked what had been a determined comeback bid by the Russians.
Trailing 3-1 entering the final period, Russia stormed back through goals by Alexander Prokopiev and Ottawa Senators' Alexei Yashin.
In the opening period the Czechs jumped out to a 2-0 lead with goals by Rostislav Vlach and Vladimir Vujtek.

Alexander Korolyk got one back for the Russians before the end of the period only to have Martin Prochazka restore the Czechs two-goal advantage early in the second with his seventh of the championship.
